title: Every account and tool, ready on day one
goal: You will sign in to work email, chat, documents, and your password manager, then install and verify your development environment.
prerequisites: Your company email address and temporary password
Your company onboarding or invitation email

steps.action: Sign in to your company email account with the address and temporary password provided by your employer.
steps.where: Google Chrome address bar and your company email provider's Sign in page.
steps.why: Your inbox contains the invitations needed to activate the other tools.
steps.checkpoint: You should see your work inbox with your company email address or profile icon in the top-right corner.
hint_levels: Start with the web address your employer gave you for email.
Open that address in Chrome, then use the Sign in form for your work account.
Click the Chrome address bar, enter the company email URL, press Enter, click Sign in, enter your work email and temporary password, then complete any prompts.

steps.action: Complete the security setup prompt for your work account using your phone.
steps.where: Security setup or More information required page displayed after email sign-in.
steps.why: Multifactor authentication protects your account and may be required before other services will open.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a success message and then return to your inbox.
hint_levels: Look for the security prompt shown after you sign in.
Choose the phone or authenticator option required by your employer and follow the code prompts.
Click Next on the security setup page, select the required method, scan the QR code or enter your phone number, confirm the displayed code, then click Done.

steps.action: Open the chat invitation in your inbox and activate your company chat account.
steps.where: Inbox message list, chat invitation email, and its Join, Accept Invitation, or Get Started button.
steps.why: Activating chat lets you communicate with your team on your first day.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the company workspace name and a list of channels or conversations in the chat app.
hint_levels: Search your newest messages for a chat or workspace invitation.
Open the invitation from Slack, Microsoft Teams, or your employer's chat service and use its activation button.
In the inbox search box, type "invitation", open the chat invitation, click Join or Accept Invitation, sign in with your work email, and follow the workspace prompts.

steps.action: Open the document-suite invitation or company portal and sign in with your work account.
steps.where: Inbox invitation message or company portal, then the Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 app launcher.
steps.why: This gives you access to the shared documents used by your team.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the document home page with your work profile icon and at least one shared or recent file area.
hint_levels: Look for a documents, Drive, SharePoint, or Microsoft 365 invitation.
Use the invitation link, then confirm that your work account appears in the document service.
Open the document-suite email, click Open, Get Started, or Accept Invitation, sign in with your work email, then open Drive or OneDrive from the app launcher.

steps.action: Open one shared onboarding document from the document home page.
steps.where: Google Drive Shared with me panel or Microsoft 365 OneDrive Shared navigation item.
steps.why: Opening a shared file verifies that your document permissions work.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the onboarding document's contents and your work profile icon in the document editor.
hint_levels: Check the area for files other people shared with you.
Open Shared with me in Drive or Shared in OneDrive and find a file with onboarding or welcome in its name.
In Google Drive click Shared with me, or in OneDrive click Shared, then double-click the onboarding file.

steps.action: Open the password-manager invitation in your inbox and create your account.
steps.where: Inbox invitation email and the Create Account, Join, or Accept Invitation button on the password manager's setup page.
steps.why: The password manager stores unique work credentials securely.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the password manager vault with your company name or work account visible.
hint_levels: Return to your inbox and find the security or password-vault invitation.
Open the invitation from 1Password, Bitwarden, or your employer's password manager and complete its account form.
Open the password-manager invitation, click Join or Accept Invitation, enter the requested account details, save the recovery information in the approved location, and click Create Account.

steps.action: Install the password manager's Chrome extension from its official Chrome Web Store listing.
steps.where: Chrome Web Store extension page and the blue Add to Chrome button.
steps.why: The extension can fill saved work credentials without copying passwords.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the password manager icon in Chrome's Extensions menu, marked by the puzzle-piece icon.
hint_levels: Look for the browser-extension option inside your password manager vault.
Use only the official extension listing published by your password-manager company.
Open the official Chrome Web Store listing, click Add to Chrome, click Add extension, then click the puzzle-piece Extensions icon and find the password manager.

steps.action: Download and run the company-approved development environment installer from the link in your onboarding materials.
steps.where: Onboarding document's development setup link, Chrome Downloads button, and the Windows installer dialog.
steps.why: The approved installer provides the editor or workstation tools required for your job.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the development app's welcome screen after installation finishes.
hint_levels: Return to the onboarding document and find the development or engineering setup section.
Use its approved Windows download link, then open the downloaded installer from Chrome.

Click the development-tool link in the onboarding document, click Download for Windows, click Chrome's Downloads button in the top-right, click the downloaded .exe file, approve the Windows prompt, and complete the installer.

steps.action: Sign in to the development app with your company-approved work account.
steps.where: Development app Welcome screen, Accounts or profile icon, and Sign In menu.
steps.why: Signing in connects your licensed features, settings, and company resources.
steps.checkpoint: You should see your work account name or email beside the app's Accounts or profile icon.
hint_levels: Find the person-shaped profile or Accounts control in the development app.
Choose the sign-in provider named in your onboarding document and use your work account.
Click the Accounts or profile icon, click Sign In, select the approved provider, complete sign-in in Chrome, then return to the development app.

steps.action: Run the onboarding document's verification command in the development app's terminal.
steps.where: Development app menu bar under Terminal > New Terminal, then the terminal panel at the bottom of the window.
steps.why: The verification command confirms that the required work environment is installed and available.
steps.checkpoint: You should see the expected version number or success message specified in the onboarding document without a command-not-found error.
hint_levels: Use the final verification command shown in the development setup section.
Open the app's integrated terminal, type the command exactly as written, and run it.
Click Terminal, click New Terminal, copy the verification command from the onboarding document, paste it into the terminal panel, and press Enter.
